pr_title: [PERF] TSDB: Query head and ooo-head together
pr_body:
The current implementation of out-of-order querying runs two queriers which each iterate all series in the head, then runs a merge operation on the output.

This PR adds `HeadAndOOOQuerier` which iterates just once over series, then where necessary merges chunks from in-order and out-of-order lists.

In order to distinguish in-order from out-of-order chunk references I set bit 23 (i.e. 1<<23) on ooo references; this reduces the maximum number of chunks from 16 million to 8 million.

Note one side-effect of this change is that results may come in a different order - the merge operation done previously required a sort of all series.  This only changes where Prometheus does not guarantee the order.

Fixes #11628

I added a benchmark showing the improvement in out-of-order querying.
It is based on the existing `BenchmarkQuerierSelect`, which seems a little odd, but serves the purpose.
Another benchmark is shown at https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/11628#issuecomment-2194345348

pr_comments:
> I am surprised we cannot simplify more code given that chunk ID (ref) holds info about OOO or not

Challenge accepted.  I removed `OOORangeHead`, `OOOHeadChunkReader` and `OOOHeadIndexReader`, so now there is `headIndexReader`, `HeadAndOOOIndexReader` and `OOOCompactionHeadIndexReader` which reads purely OOO samples.

We still have a bit of bulk in `HeadAndOOOQuerier` and `HeadAndOOOChunkQuerier`, which are broadly doing what `blockQuerier` and `blockChunkQuerier` do, but it is proving hard to bring them all back together.
Rebased again to resolve conflict with #14438

I have made most of the changes that @colega suggested.  
Still thinking about the last one.
Also rebased and squashed some commits.

issue_context.title: Reuse the postings index when head and ooo head are overlapped
issue_context.body:
### Proposal

Currently, the head index and the ooo head index are the same, when both head and ooo head fall into the same query range, we can reuse the postings index to avoid duplicate computation and reduce memory usage.
comments: Do you have a benchmark that illustrates the problem?

I am talking about this in theory, the [PostingsForMatchers](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/30b31cae93b2fe66486f188c07e215b80ebc93f8/tsdb/querier.go#L228) will be executed twice if both heads fall into the same query range.

I would like to hear more constructive input before I write any code.
My constructive feedback is to show a benchmark.

@bboreham I can't follow you, and with my limited experience, I am hoping you explain the "benchmark" a little bit, is there anything we can talk about before a real benchmark? Ideas, experiences, and numbers in theory could be helpful.
@bboreham As you wish, I have submitted #11644 with a benchmark to illustrate the problem, I hope that you find it useful, and maybe give some advice and ideas based on the patch.

I have another idea, which I shall call `ActiveQueryPostingsCache`. This cache will be available only to active(running) queries. However, there may be abnormal queries that remain active indefinitely. For such situations, we need to enforce a duration of validity. We modify the `Querier.Select(...) XSet` to `Querier.Select(...) (XSet, func())` to conduct appropriate cleanup work. The cleanup process will remove the cache entry when the reference count decreases to zero, ensuring that the postings cache remains valid during the entire lifetime of that query. As stated before, we will enforce a duration of validity to prevent caches from retaining their validity for an excessive amount of time.

> abnormal queries that remain active indefinitely

Can you explain how this happens?

> > abnormal queries that remain active indefinitely
> 
> Can you explain how this happens?

Perhaps I should quote the 'abnormal'.

Some clients may periodically send identical queries, such as recording rules. Assuming the interval is 5 seconds, if the query execution exceeds this duration, the postings cache from the head may remain valid indefinitely, thus causing problems.

Thanks for creating a benchmark. From profiling it seems that most of the work is in merging two sets of series.  And in fact they are actually the same set of series.

This led me to think of another way to solve the problem: create an iterator that walks the series for both head and OOO-head, and merges just the chunks.  This would avoid any cache lifetime issues.

[Returning to this because I noticed a related issue in a production system at work - it spent a lot of time executing regexps, and it did the same work for head and ooo-head.]

review_comments:
I understand that we don't want to run a check here for every chunk, but what if pos+firstOOOChunkID overflow to that bit 23? 

Since `pos < len(s.ooo.oooMmappedChunks)`, maybe we could do the check when we `mmapCurrentOOOHeadChunk`?
Sounds like we need to update commentary here to include masking and what it's for?

Is it really worth having this as a separate chunk querier at this point? All OOO logic is only executed after checking simple conditions like `s.ooo != nil` or `isOOO`, maybe this could be _the only head querier_?

Maybe we can do that as a follow up PR and measure the impact separately.
no, that would ignore out of order chunks.
Method name sounds like it will get OOO series chunks, but it gets all series chunks, including OOO. What about calling it `getSeriesChunksWithOOO`?
